mechanism_narrative: A sustained quarterly decline in FEDFUNDS signals an easing monetary policy cycle, which reduces discount rates on equity cash flows, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) during FEDFUNDS decline, or the relationship weakens in non-easing cycles.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in UNRATE below 3.5% triggers increased labor market optimism, boosting equity valuations and generating positive S&P 500 forward returns within 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) when UNRATE crosses below 3.5%, or the effect persists without a clear labor market response.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent quarterly growth in GDPC1 (demand) and contraction in INDPRO (supply) creates upward pressure on asset prices, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The interaction effect does not predict significant positive returns (p > 0.05) over 60 days, or the relationship reverses during contractionary phases.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime, a sustained decline in FEDFUNDS accelerates growth expectations, amplifying S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) during FEDFUNDS declines in late-cycle periods, or the effect diminishes outside this regime.

mechanism_narrative: Sustained monthly increases in INDPRO (supply) reflect robust economic output, boosting corporate earnings and equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) during INDPRO growth, or the relationship weakens in contractionary phases.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in FEDFUNDS above 2.5% signals aggressive monetary tightening, reducing growth prospects and generating negative S&P 500 forward returns within 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during FEDFUNDS spikes above 2.5%, or the effect reverses in non-tightening phases.

mechanism_narrative: Rising PAYEMS (labor demand) coupled with strong GDPC1 (economic demand) creates a virtuous cycle of wage growth and corporate investment, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The combined effect of PAYEMS and GDPC1 does not predict significant positive returns (p > 0.05) over 20 days, or the interaction weakens in contractionary labor markets.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle, rising FEDFUNDS rates reduce growth expectations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during FEDFUNDS rises in tightening cycles, or the effect reverses outside this regime.
